arxiv-1807-02012.title: Correlated long-range mixed-harmonic fluctuations measured in p ​ p pp , p p +Pb and low-multiplicity Pb+Pb collisions with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-1807-02012.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1807-02012.description: Abstract Correlations of two flow harmonics v n v_{n} and v m v_{m} via three- and four-particle cumulants are measured in 13 TeV p ​ p pp , 5.02 TeV p p +Pb, and 2.76 TeV peripheral Pb+Pb collisions with the ATLAS detector at the LHC.

arxiv-2103-08551.title: A fully local hybridised second-order accurate scheme for advection-diffusion equations
arxiv-2103-08551.creator: Hanz Martin Cheng
arxiv-2103-08551.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hanz Martin Cheng. In this paper, we present a fully local second-order upwind scheme, applicable on generic meshes. This is done by hybridisation, which is achieved by introducing unknowns on each edge of the mesh. By doing so, fluxes only depend on values associated to a single cell, and thus, this scheme can easily be applied even on cells near the boundary of the domain. Another advantage of hybridised schemes is that static condensation can be employed, leading to a very efficient implementation.

arxiv-2103-12167.title: Fano–Mukai fourfolds of genus 10 10 and their automorphism groups Thanks: The research of the first author was partially supported by the HSE University Basic Research Program.
arxiv-2103-12167.creator: Yuri Prokhorov, Mikhail Zaidenberg
arxiv-2103-12167.description: Abstract . The automorphism groups of the Fano–Mukai fourfold of genus 10 10 were studied in our previous paper [ PZ18 ] . In particular, we found in [ PZ18 ] the neutral components of these groups. In the present paper we finish the description of the discrete parts.

arxiv-2104-08981.title: History of Prime Movers and Future Implications
arxiv-2104-08981.creator: Mikhail V. Shubov
arxiv-2104-08981.description: Abstract Abstract Motive and electrical energy has played a crucial role in human civilization. Since Ancient times, motive energy played a primary role in agricultural and industrial production as well as transportation. At that time, motive energy was provided by work of humans and draft animals. Later, work of water and wind power was harnessed.

arxiv-2107-10705.title: Thermodynamics of light management in near-field thermophotovoltaics
arxiv-2107-10705.creator: Georgia T. Papadakis, Meir Orenstein, Eli Yablonovitch, Shanhui Fan
arxiv-2107-10705.description: Abstract We evaluate near-field thermophotovoltaic (TPV) energy conversion systems focusing in particular on their open-circuit voltage ( V oc V_{\mathrm{oc}} ). Unlike previous analyses based largely on numerical simulations with fluctuational electrodynamics, here, we develop an analytic model that captures the physics of near-field TPV systems and can predict their performance metrics.

arxiv-2205-07933.title: DiuSST: A conceptual model of diurnal warm layers for idealized atmospheric simulations with interactive SST
arxiv-2205-07933.description: Abstract The diurnal variability of sea surface temperature (SST) may play an important role for cloud organization above the tropical ocean, with implications for precipitation extremes, storminess, and climate sensitivity. Recent cloud-resolving simulations demonstrate how imposed diurnal SST oscillations can strongly, and delicately, impact mesoscale convective organization.

arxiv-2302-04862.title: Polynomial Neural Fields for Subband Decomposition and Manipulation
arxiv-2302-04862.creator: Guandao Yang, Sagie Benaim *, Varun Jampani, Kyle Genova, Jonathan T. Barron, Thomas Funkhouser, Bharath Hariharan, Serge Belongie
arxiv-2302-04862.description: Abstract Neural fields have emerged as a new paradigm for representing signals, thanks to their ability to do it compactly while being easy to optimize. In most applications, however, neural fields are treated like black boxes, which precludes many signal manipulation tasks. In this paper, we propose a new class of neural fields called polynomial neural fields (PNFs).

arxiv-2307-08746.title: Unravelling the structure of magnetised molecular clouds with SILCC-Zoom: sheets, filaments and fragmentation 2022 Unravelling the structure of magnetised molecular clouds with SILCC-Zoom: sheets, filaments and fragmentation – F
arxiv-2307-08746.creator: Shashwata Ganguly, S. Walch, D. Seifried, S. D. Clarke, M. Weis
arxiv-2307-08746.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shashwata Ganguly, S. Walch, D. Seifried, S. D. Clarke, M. Weis. To what extent magnetic fields affect how molecular clouds (MCs) fragment and create dense structures is an open question. We present a numerical study of cloud fragmentation using the SILCC-Zoom simulations. These simulations follow the self-consistent formation of MCs in a few hundred parsec sized region of a stratified galactic disc; and include magnetic fields, self-gravity, supernova-driven turbulence, as well as a non-equilibrium chemical network.

arxiv-2403-09643.title: An Umbral Extension of the General Leibniz Product rule for Fractional Indices and Applications
arxiv-2403-09643.creator: Ryan Mahendra Wilis
arxiv-2403-09643.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ryan Mahendra Wilis. An Algebraic Extension of the General Leibniz Product rule for Fractional Indices and Applications

Ryan Mahendra Wilis

Abstract

This paper presents a reformulation of the Leibniz product rule as a finite sum that expresses the fractional derivative of the product of two differentiable functions.

arxiv-2405-14799.title: Exploring modified Kaniadakis entropy: MOND theory and the Bekenstein bound conjecture
arxiv-2405-14799.creator: Gabriella V. Ambrósio, Michelly S. Andrade, Paulo R. F. Alves, Cleber N. Costa, Jorge Ananias Neto, Ronaldo Thibes
arxiv-2405-14799.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gabriella V. Ambrósio, Michelly S. Andrade, Paulo R. F. Alves, Cleber N. Costa, Jorge Ananias Neto, Ronaldo Thibes. We examine the potential of Kaniadakis entropy to describe black-hole entropy, proposing a modified version accounting for black hole thermodynamics. We posit a conjecture that the Kaniadakis entropy precisely describes the Bekenstein-Hawking black-hole entropy. Additionally, we discuss the Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) theory, a modification of Newton’s second law aimed at explaining galaxy rotation curves without resorting to dark matter.

arxiv-2511-00240.title: A Milky Way mass model for isolated simulations
arxiv-2511-00240.creator: J. A. Sellwood
arxiv-2511-00240.description: Abstract This paper presents an equilibrium model of a Milky Way-like spiral galaxy that supports open, mostly 2- and 3-arm spiral patterns but does not form a bar. It is suggested as a more realistic alternative model to that employed by the agora collaboration; their model has a much lower disk mass and therefore forms only multi-arm spiral patterns.

arxiv-2511-05166.title: Cosmological perturbations in Energy-Momentum Squared Gravity
arxiv-2511-05166.creator: Peter K. S. Dunsby 1,2,3, Maria-Alexia Caldis 1, Eduardo Bittencourt 4
arxiv-2511-05166.description: Abstract We present a fully covariant and gauge–invariant analysis of linear cosmological perturbations in Energy–Momentum Squared Gravity. Working within the + 3 1\!+\!3 formalism, we derive the exact propagation equations for scalar, vector, and tensor modes on FLRW backgrounds, in the case of radiation and dust.

arxiv-2511-13921.title: Multi-layered Fast Wind observed in XMM-Newton snapshot of Seyfert 1 Markarian 877
arxiv-2511-13921.creator: Xin Xiang, Jon M. Miller, Ehud Behar, W. N. Brandt, Luigi Gallo, Doyee Byun, Elena Gallo
arxiv-2511-13921.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xin Xiang, Jon M. Miller, Ehud Behar, W. N. Brandt, Luigi Gallo, Doyee Byun, Elena Gallo. Ultra Fast Outflows (UFOs) are powerful, highly ionized winds launched from the innermost regions of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs), reaching velocities of 0.03 – 0.3 c and playing a key role in AGN feedback.

arxiv-2601-09694.title: LLMs can Compress LLMs: Adaptive Pruning by Agents
arxiv-2601-09694.creator: Sai Varun Kodathala (✉), Rakesh Vunnam
arxiv-2601-09694.description: Abstract As Large Language Models (LLMs) continue to scale, post-training pruning has emerged as a promising approach to reduce computational costs while preserving performance. Existing methods such as SparseGPT and Wanda achieve high sparsity through layer-wise weight reconstruction or activation-aware magnitude pruning, but rely on uniform or hand-crafted heuristics to determine per-layer sparsity ratios.

arxiv-2601-20866.title: Cramér-Rao Bound Analysis and Near-Optimal Performance of the Synchronous Nyquist-Folding Generalized Eigenvalue Method (SNGEM) for Sub-Nyquist Multi-Tone Parameter Estimation
arxiv-2601-20866.creator: Huiguang Zhang
arxiv-2601-20866.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Huiguang Zhang. The Synchronous Nyquist-folding Generalized Eigenvalue Method (SNGEM) achieves full frequency/amplitude/phase estimation for multi-tone signals at extreme sub-Nyquist rates by jointly processing the original signal and its time-derivative (differential channel). This paper derives the exact Cramér-Rao bound for the amplitude-ratio parameter R = A / B = 1 / ( 2 ​ π ​ f ) R=A/B=1/(2\pi f) under equal-SNR dual-channel Gaussian noise.

plos-pone-0006559.creator: George Jiang, Meng Shi, Solomon Conteh et al.
plos-pone-0006559.description: PLOS ONE research article. Using newer vaccine platforms which have been effective against malaria in rodent models, we tested five immunization regimens against Plasmodium knowlesi in rhesus monkeys. All vaccines included the same four P. knowlesi antigens: the pre-erythrocytic antigens CSP, SSP2, and ery

pmc-11322531.title: Altering traits and fates of wild populations with Mendelian DNA sequence modifying Allele Sails
pmc-11322531.creator: Michelle L Johnson, Bruce A Hay, Maciej Maselko
pmc-11322531.description: Population-scale genome modification can alter the composition or fate of wild populations. Synthetic gene drives provide one set of tools, but their use is complicated by scientific, regulatory, and social issues associated with transgene persistence and flow. Here we propose an alternative approach.

pmc-11479314.title: A Tunnel Fire Detection Method Based on an Improved Dempster-Shafer Evidence Theory
pmc-11479314.creator: Haiying Wang, Yuke Shi, Long Chen, Xiaofeng Zhang, Michele Penza
pmc-11479314.description: Tunnel fires are generally detected using various sensors, including measuring temperature, CO concentration, and smoke concentration. To address the ambiguity and inconsistency in multi-sensor data, this paper proposes a tunnel fire detection method based on an improved Dempster-Shafer (DS) evidence theory for multi-sensor data fusion.

pmc-13403384.title: Comparative Genomic Analysis Uncovers the Evolutionary Basis of Siliceous Cell Wall Formation Across Diverse Lineages
pmc-13403384.creator: Limin Jia, Liangwei Li, Yaolei Zhang, Jiahao Wang, Zengbao Yuan, Guangyi Fan, Chengcheng Shi, Man Zhang
pmc-13403384.description: Simple SummarySiliceous cell walls are key biomineralization structures in eukaryotes, particularly in diatoms, but their evolutionary origins remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified 75 orthogroups universally conserved across 57 species (representing eight taxonomic groups), and an additional 105 orthogroups consistently present across four silica-bearing lineages (Bacillariophyta, Parmales, choanoflagellates, and Bacillus), mainly associated with fundamental metabolism.
